title: He fed them.
paragraphs:
He fed them.
Led them.
Bled for them…
…and one of the sheep bit Him.
Let that image disturb you for a second.

Not a wolf.
Not a stranger.
A sheep.

The very one He carried on His shoulders.
The very one He protected when danger came.
The very one who knew His voice.

Still—
it bit Him.
There’s a kind of pain that only comes from those you love.

Not the criticism from outsiders.
Not the attacks from enemies.

But the quiet betrayal…
from people who once called you home.

If you’ve ever poured your life into someone—
prayed for them,
believed in them,
walked with them through their darkest valleys—
…and then one day, they turned on you…
You understand this story.
But here’s where it goes deeper.
This isn’t just your story.
This is the story of Jesus Christ.

He didn’t just experience rejection.
He embraced it—knowing it would come.

He sat at the table…
broke bread…
looked into the eyes of the one who would betray Him…
…and still chose love.
“He who shares my bread has lifted up his heel against me.” — John 13:18

That wasn’t an accident.
That wasn’t surprise.
That was foreknown pain… met with intentional grace.
Let me speak straight to your heart.
Some of you are bleeding right now.

Not physically—
but emotionally, spiritually.

You were loyal…
but they walked away.

You were faithful…
but they misunderstood you.

You stayed…
but they left.
And now there’s a question echoing inside you:
“Was it worth it?”
Look at the Shepherd.
Look at Christ.

He was bitten…
betrayed…
denied…
abandoned…
…and still went to the cross.
Why?

Because His mission was never based on their response.
It was anchored in His love.
Because there’s another layer.
Sometimes… we are not the wounded shepherd.
Sometimes…
we are the sheep that bite.

We resist correction.
We question motives.
We withdraw when truth confronts us.
We take offense instead of taking responsibility.

We say we want guidance—
but we reject authority.

We say we want growth—
but we avoid surrender.

We say we love God—
but ignore His voice.
And in subtle, quiet ways…
we bite the very hand that feeds us.
That’s uncomfortable.
But it’s honest.
And the Gospel is not afraid of honesty.
Here’s the turning point.
This is where religion would shame you.
But Jesus?
He does something different.
He doesn’t discard the sheep.
He doesn’t cancel the betrayer.
He doesn’t walk away from the broken.
He goes to the cross.
Voluntarily.
Fully aware.
Fully surrendered.
“I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.” — John 10:11
Not for perfect sheep.
Not for loyal sheep.
Not for easy sheep.
For biting sheep.
That’s the scandal.
That’s the beauty.
That’s the Gospel.

You can wound Him—
and He will still reach for you.

You can fail Him—
and He will still forgive you.

You can run from Him—
and He will still pursue you.
But grace is not permission to stay the same.

Grace is an invitation to come back…
changed.
So here’s the question you can’t ignore:

Are you the wounded…
or the one who wounded?

Are you carrying pain…
or causing it?
Maybe both.
Then hear this clearly:
There is room at the cross for both.

For the betrayed—
there is healing.

For the betrayer—
there is mercy.
But the response matters.

Not denial.
Not excuses.
Not pride.
Repentance.
A turning of the heart.
A surrender of the will.
A return to the Shepherd.
Because the cross doesn’t just expose sin.
It provides the way out.
Through Jesus alone.

Not self-improvement.
Not religious effort.
Not trying harder.
Only Him.
So if your heart is heavy…
If your spirit feels torn…
If you’re tired of the cycle of hurting and being hurt…
Come back.
Not to religion.
Not to performance.
But to a Person.
Jesus Christ.
He is not waiting to crush you.
He’s waiting to restore you.
The scars in His hands are not weapons.
They are reminders.
You were worth staying for.
You were worth dying for.
You are still worth redeeming.
And maybe…
just maybe…
the one who bit the Shepherd…
can become the one who follows Him again.
Sit with it.
Because someone out there is bleeding silently…
and someone else doesn’t even realize they’ve been biting.
Come home.
